question: Do the live LLM alert filter's stored suppressions, overall and per reason category, block signals that are better or worse than average under the E0 rules?
seen: The untracked filter316 campaign (https://github.com/mfittko/market-signals/issues/316#issuecomment-6055138146) already scored these verdicts under a different management. This run is a reproduction on frozen exports and no independent test.

export.rule: signals left-joined to signal_snapshots on instrument, granularity and time; flip rows only (kind supertrend-flip or null); verdict alert or suppress; instrument WTICO/USD; time before 2026-10-01T00:00:00.000Z; columns instrument,granularity,time,signal,verdict,reason,filter_model
export.label: measured
export.source: the owner's one-time read-only sqlite3 export of data/candles.db, query in https://github.com/mfittko/market-signals/issues/316; sha256 by shasum -a 256; 2,013 data rows: M1 499 alert and 1,194 suppress, M5 102 alert and 218 suppress

granularities.rule: M1, M5, M15 and H1 are scored; a bar of each starts at the floor of the M1 bar time to 60, 300, 900 or 3600 seconds since the Unix epoch; any other granularity is excluded as unsupported_granularity
granularities.label: assumed
granularities.source: issue 316 Approach; filter316 prereg data.outcomes: M5/M15/H1 by bars.resample of M1

categories.rule: multi-label, case-insensitive regex search on the suppression reason; a suppression carries every category whose regex matches; a suppression with no match is other; allowed signals carry no category
categories.label: assumed

list.name: low_volume
list.regex: thin|low[- ]vol|weak[- ]vol|sub-?average|below[- ]av(era)?ge?|light vol|avg vol|average vol|\b0?\.\d+ ?[x×]|\(0\.\d+\)|ratio 0|vol(ume)? (only |of )?(0|1\.[0-4])\d*|no volume|volume not

exclusions.rule: checked in this order: fail_open (reason starts with 'filter error'), unsupported_granularity, unmatched (no E0 trade with the signal time as flip time and the signal side as direction, E0 holds included), censored (the joined trade's exit reason is end); every other verdict is scored with the joined trade's net R
exclusions.label: assumed

days.rule: a signal's day is the UTC calendar date of its time; the bootstrap resamples the ascending list of distinct days that hold at least one scored signal
days.label: assumed
days.source: issue 316 Approach (UTC trading days); filter316 used 22:00 UTC sessions and kept days without rows

thinningDraws.label: assumed
thinningDraws.source: filter316 prereg metrics.null: 500 uniform draws of the same blocked count

seed.label: assumed
seed.source: fixed here before the first run; one PCG stream seeds the bootstrap and then the random thinning

ci.rule: the 2.5th and 97.5th percentiles, linear interpolation, of the bootstrap replicates of a statistic; a replicate where the statistic is undefined is dropped
ci.label: assumed

delta.rule: per rule: delta = mean net R of the blocked signals minus mean net R of all scored signals; the random-thinning percentile is the share of thinning deltas below the observed delta
delta.label: assumed

decisionRule.keep: blocked >= minBlocked and the delta CI upper bound is below 0: the rule blocks worse-than-average signals
decisionRule.drop: blocked >= minBlocked and the delta CI lower bound is above 0: the rule blocks better-than-average signals
decisionRule.lateChasing: late_chasing delta CI lower bound above 0: blocks better-than-average signals; upper bound below 0: worse-than-average; else not distinguishable from average
decisionRule.thinning: the random-thinning percentile is reported as a comparison and does not enter the decision
decisionRule.label: assumed
decisionRule.source: issue 316 Approach; no multiple-comparison correction (issue 316 non-goals)

reference.label: measured
reference.differences: filter316 used another management (1.5 ATR stop, breakeven after 1 R, 3 R target, opposite flip exit, 72-bar horizon, overlapping trades allowed) and another population (all live instruments with bid/ask history except DE30/EUR, 2026-07-22 to 2026-10-08). Its random-thinning percentile ranks kept-minus-all, which falls when blocked-minus-all rises, so it reads roughly as 100 minus the percentile here. Its keep rule also needed the null q97.5 and a Holm-adjusted p below 0.05.
summary: Scored: 5,455 signals over 61 trading days; 1,007 allowed, 4,448 suppressed (82%).
